name: Example: Proving the Matrix Exponential Formula for IVP Solution of an Inhomogeneous System
problem:
Consider the inhomogeneous system  $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. A derivation of the formula for the solution $\mathbf{x}(t)$ passing through $\mathbf{x}(t_0)$ is presented below.

$\textrm{L1}{:}\;$ Let $\mathbf{y}(t)=e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t)$  

$\textrm{L2}{:}\;$ $\mathbf{y}'(t) = -Ae^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t) + e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}'(t)$  

$\textrm{L3}{:}\;$ $\mathbf{y}'(t)=e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{g}(t)$  

$\textrm{L4}{:}\;$ $\displaystyle\mathbf{y}(t)-\mathbf{y}(t_0) = \int_{t_0}^{t} e^{-A(s-t_0)}\mathbf{g}(s) \, \text{d}s$

$\textrm{L5}{:}\;$ $\mathbf{y}(t_0)=\mathbf{x}(t_0)$ 

$\textrm{L6}{:}\;$ $\displaystyle\mathbf{y}(t)=\mathbf{x}(t_0)+\int_{t_0}^{t} e^{-A(s-t_0)}\mathbf{g}(s) \, \text{d}s$  

$\textrm{L7}{:}\;$ $\displaystyle e^{A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{y}(t)=e^{A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t_0)+\int_{t_0}^{t} e^{A(t-s)}\mathbf{g}(s) \, \text{d}s$

$\textrm{L8}{:}\;$ $e^{A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{y}(t)=\mathbf{x}(t)$

$\textrm{L9}{:}\;$ $\displaystyle\mathbf{x}(t)=e^{A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t_0)+\int_{t_0}^{t} e^{A(t-s)}\mathbf{g}(s) \, \text{d}s$

Fill in the blanks with the correct reasons to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\quad$ Line $\textrm{L3}$ follows from $\textrm{L2}$ by  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/befe715ac2d9375061b1a3c8c0528a0bfb2764197cee4eca4d2b60146cec20b6.png).

$\quad$ Line $\textrm{L5}$ follows from line $\textrm{L1}$ by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/09febb48bb00d22caebf088103181b5db6377befccad18f1370718351cc91e9d.png).

$\quad$ Line $\textrm{L8}$ follows from line $\textrm{L1}$ by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/999db06dcfe0878ddb3316b11546668ba9442d8fd110165e5076b90964b84905.png).
worked_solution:
Let's justify each of the selected steps.

- We first consider lines $\textrm{L2}$ and $\textrm{L3}.$ Starting from

$$
\mathbf{y}'(t) = -Ae^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t) + e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}'(t)
$$

in $\textrm{L2}$ and substituting $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t)$ from the original system gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =-A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}(Ax(t)+g(t)) \\  & =-A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}g(t) \\  & ={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}g(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $\textrm{L3}$ follows from $\textrm{L2}$ by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/9dcfd90e4444195ee781ab388b36a575ec1219d1820f7141114e29311941ddc5.png)

- Next, we consider lines $\textrm{L1}$ and $\textrm{L5}.$ Evaluating $\mathbf{y}(t)=e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t)$ at $t=t_0$ gives

$$
\mathbf{y}(t_0)=e^{-A(t_0-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t_0)=I\mathbf{x}(t_0)=\mathbf{x}(t_0).
$$

Therefore, $\textrm{L5}$ follows from line $\textrm{L1}$  by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/90a07cffb30b2ef860b0d3314865a7bd9ca0b7c86811a63b07628c768188af3e.png)

- Finally, we consider lines $\textrm{L1}$ and $\textrm{L8}.$ Multiplying both sides of

$$
\mathbf{y}(t)=e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t)
$$

from $\textrm{L1}$ by $e^{A(t-t_0)}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}y(t) & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t) \\  & =x(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\textrm{L8}$ follows from $\textrm{L1}$ by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071250/assets/23a2ac9e75c9bac22187814f524d919166d3748f1caa5831d664231a80bac296.png)
